c:
A six-note piano cadence chill, / The Shape stands on the autumn hill;
Behind the pale William Shatner mask, / He finishes his butchering task.
“A boy’s best friend is his mother.” Forty thousand stolen dollars vanish into the fruit cellar, accompanied by screeching violins in a shower stall.
Who am I? — Unearthed from Nineveh ruins, my demonic presence manifests in a Georgetown child with spinning head, levitating mattress, and foul vomit, mocking the rites of two Jesuit priests.
“What’s your favorite scary movie?” A ghost-faced caller weaponizes slasher cliches over a cellular phone, hunting teenagers who break the cardinal rules of horror.

They only moved the granite stones, / Leaving the subterranean bones;
Through static television snow, / The hungry closet demons glow.
“Here’s Johnny!” An isolated winter caretaker’s writer's block erupts into manic axe swings, elevator torrents of crimson, and frozen hedge maze footprints.
Who am I? — Paralyzed by a silver spoon tapping porcelain china, I fall helpless into the black Sunken Place while an affluent upstate family auctions my body for neurosurgical theft.

A static tape of wells and trees, / A telephone chime on the breeze;
Seven days the clock shall run, / Till water crawls into the sun.
Who am I? — In a 1922 silent masterwork, my clawed, rodent-like shadow ascends the whitewashed stair of Bremen, sailing upon a ghost ship laden with plague-bearing vermin.
“Why are they doing this? Why are they gathering?” Innocently purchased caged lovebirds trigger an unexplained avian apocalypse, turning telephone wires into perches of death.

Near Gargantua’s titanic ring, / One hour will seven winters bring;
Through gravitational morse he speaks, / Behind the bookshelf that she seeks.
“You take the blue pill, the story ends. You take the red pill, you stay in Wonderland, and I show you how deep the rabbit hole goes.”

Neon rain on Los Angeles street, / Where rogue synthetic humans meet;
“All those moments lost in pain, / Like tears dissolved inside the rain.”
Who am I? — In zero-gravity hotel hallways and snowbound mountain vaults, I stage corporate espionage within dreams, relying on a perpetual brass spinning top to know if I am awake.
“If you could see your whole life from start to finish, would you change things?” Circular inky glyphs unlock a palindromic timeline, uniting a daughter’s birth with her future demise.

Who am I? — Gestating inside a commercial towing crewman after an eggsack breach, my acid-blooded biomechanical perfection erupts through the chest to hunt in steam vents where no one can hear you scream.
“I’ll be back.” A hyperalloy cybernetic assassin wrapped in living human tissue storms a police station to exterminate the mother of the future resistance.

Prehistoric amber preserved the flea, / To patch the gaps with amphibian spree;
When stormy winds cut electric strand, / Colossal reptiles rule the land.
Who am I? — In Fritz Lang’s 1927 silent dystopia, I am the metallic robot built in the likeness of Maria, inciting subterranean workers to drown their own machinery in catastrophic revolt.
“Isn’t it strange, to create something that hates you?” A translucent silicone android manipulates power blackouts and an insecure coder to escape her creator's glass prison.

A clucking tongue, a severed head, / A miniature diorama of the dead;
In candlelit attics bowing prone, / King Paimon mounts his fleshy throne.
Who am I? — Crowned in an enormous pyramid of meadow blossoms after psychedelic dancing in perpetual Swedish sunlight, I smile as an unfaithful lover burns inside a hollowed-out bear carcass.
“Why’d ya spill yer beans, Tommy?” Two wickies trapped on a storm-lashed New England spit drink kerosene, murder seagulls, and lust after the blinding lantern light.
“Wouldst thou like the taste of butter? A pretty dress? Wouldst thou like to live deliciously?” whispers Black Phillip in the moonlit New England woods.

Upon the white sand path tread light, / Speak not a syllable in the night;
For blind monstrosities attend, / To every whisper silence would end.
“Well, Clarice… have the lambs stopped screaming?” An imprisoned cannibal psychiatrist trades psychological profiling for traumatic childhood memories.
“What’s in the box?!” screams a distraught detective in the arid desert power lines, discovering how a serial preacher orchestrated the final mortal sin of wrath.
Who am I? — Searching for a vanished inmate at an offshore fortress for the criminally insane, my migraine hallucinations and lighthouse dreams force me to realize I am the sixtieth patient.

In fascist Spain the faun awaits, / Beyond the mossy stone-hewn gates;
Beware the Pale Man's banquet hall, / Whose eyes upon his fingers crawl.
Who am I? — Sent backward from an underground post-apocalyptic future to intercept an army releasing a fatal virus, I realize the recurring airport nightmare of my childhood was my own death.

A jet turbine falls from cloudless skies, / A monstrous rabbit with silver eyes;
Twenty-eight days the clock shall chime, / To close the tangent seam of time.
“Good morning, and in case I don't see ya: good afternoon, good evening, and good night!” A cheerful insurance clerk discovers his entire world is an ocean under a domed television set.
Who am I? — In a bleak 2027 where two decades of global infertility have doomed humanity to despair, I am the miraculous young immigrant carrying the first unborn child in eighteen years.

w: ETERNAL SUNSHINE OF THE SPOTLESS MIND
c: “Meet me in Montauk…” Desperate to erase the memories of a turbulent tangerine-haired romance, a subconscious lover flees through collapsing rooms and childhood sandbars.

Two telepods in clean array, / A buzzing pest that went astray;
Flesh fused with chitin, genes defiled, / A Brundle-monster fierce and wild.

Who am I? — An extraterrestrial cellular imitator buried a hundred thousand years in polar ice, I assimilate sled dogs and Antarctic scientists, betraying my presence only when hot copper touches blood.
“You’re gonna need a bigger boat.” A twenty-five-foot rogue carcharodon terrorizes the Fourth of July beaches of Amity Island, luring the Orca into an offshore duel.
Who am I? — Stricken with anterograde memory loss since the assault that killed my wife, I navigate a reverse investigation through tattooed facts, labeled Polaroids, and self-delusion.
“The first rule of Fight Club is: you do not talk about Fight Club.” A nameless insomniac discovers his charismatic soap-peddling anarchic companion is his own nocturnal hallucination.
“I see dead people. Walking around like regular people. They don't see each other. They only see what they want to see. They don't know they're dead.”

In mirrors shattered, visions gleam, / To dance Tchaikovsky's royal dream;
From porcelain white to feathers black, / Her sanity will not come back.
“I’m your number one fan!” A bedridden novelist crippled in a Colorado snowstorm is kept prisoner by a nurse whose devotion turns to sledgehammer amputations when her heroine dies.

Keep awake and guard the light, / Do not sleep into the night;
Four sharpened blades upon his hand, / He rules the screaming slumber land.

Who am I? — A semi-basement Seoul family who falsified credentials to infiltrate an affluent architect's villa as tutors, chauffeurs, and housekeepers, unaware of the secret bunker beneath the pantry.
Who am I? — A pagan Babylonian deity known as Baghuul, I harvest children's souls through eight-millimeter snuff films discovered in an author's attic.
“The virgin survives—or she dies last! That’s all that matters!” Underground corporate technicians manipulate college archetypes into slaughter to placate ancient deities sleeping beneath the earth.

Spiraling stair and dizzy heights, / San Francisco's foggy nights;
He dyes her hair and buys the dress, / To resurrect a ghost's caress.
Who am I? — Confined to a wheelchair with a broken leg during a Greenwich Village heatwave, I peer through a telephoto lens to deduce my courtyard neighbor chopped his wife into luggage.
“Now it’s dark,” whispers Frank Booth, inhaling amyl nitrite from a mask. An innocent young man finds a severed human ear in an idyllic meadow, plummeting into neon subterranean rot.
“Why are you doing this to us?” weeping victims ask the sack-masked intruders outside their secluded vacation cabin. The chilling reply: “Because you were home.”

Red boiler suits and golden shears, / Underground echoes of our fears;
Across the continent they stand, / The Tethered shadows take the land.
“Where we’re going, we won’t need eyes to see.” An experimental gravity-drive vessel orbits Neptune, returning from an alternate dimension of pure, screaming infernal chaos.

In Black Hills woods the branches crack, / Small stick-bundle talismans on the track;
No compass turns the hunters right, / And someone stands in the corner's sight.

If it's in a word, or it's in a look, / You can't get rid of the Babadook;
A rumbling growl, three taps on the door, / A mother's grief upon the floor.
“What’s the most you ever lost on a coin toss?” An emotionless hitman carrying a pneumatic cattle stunner wagers mortal souls on the call of a nickel in west Texas.
Who am I? — A construction worker whose virtual holiday memory implant in Rekall inadvertently unmasks my true identity as an elite double-agent on a rebel-controlled Martian colony.

An unearthly vapor rolls from lake, / Where tentacled behemoths wake;
Inside the market, zealots scream, / And hasty bullets end the dream.
“We don’t want to conquer any cosmos, we want to extend the Earth to the cosmos.” Yet the sentient oceanic planet generates living physical spectres of a psychologist’s dead wife.
Who am I? — Trapped in an unmapped Appalachian cavern system by a subterranean cave-in, my spelunking expedition is hunted through pitch darkness by blind, carnivorous humanoid crawlers.

When midnight strikes the mortals sleep, / While Strangers in their trench coats creep;
They bend the stone and swap the mind, / Till one awake leaves night behind.
